author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory lists every specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only specialty directory answers the inverse of the vet list: every specialty the clinic knows, under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, on one page reached by its own address.
acceptance_criteria: Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened at /specialties.html, then every specialty is listed under its stored name.
Given a specialty one or more veterinarians hold, when the specialty directory is opened, then each of them is listed under it by first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary").
Given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears on the page nowhere.
Given a specialty the clinic knows but no veterinarian holds, when the specialty directory is opened, then it is still listed, with no veterinarian under it.
Given a veterinarian holding more than one specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian is listed under each of them.
Given every specialty the clinic knows, when the specialty directory is opened, then all of them are on the one page, with no paging.
Given the specialty directory, when it is rendered, then it carries the navigation every page carries, and no page carries a link to it.
Given the page's own wording, when any supported language is requested, then the wording is presented in it and none is fixed to a single language.
non_goals: managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged)
a navigation entry or any link from another page to the specialty directory
paging, sorting, or filtering the specialty directory
searching for a specialty or a veterinarian (NG-9, unchanged)
notes: Grounded in the intake-decision at line 1. Non-Goals table untouched, so no scope_overrides: the intake quotes NG-2 as unchanged, and NG-9 declines search rather than a listing. Two open questions recorded in docs/prd.md rather than paused on: the order specialties and veterinarians appear in (unspecified by the request, so no order is required), and whether a visible entry point follows later. REQ-SYS-001 still binds on the new page, hence the navigation criterion; REQ-LANG-002 binds on its wording. The page shows each specialty's stored name, not a translated label.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory stays inside the vet feature package and adds no module or dependency. Two facts make it new ground rather than a copy of the vet list. The Vet-to-Specialty association is mapped in one direction only (Vet.java, @ManyToMany with no inverse side), so a Specialty cannot reach its holders; and the page must list a specialty no veterinarian holds, so the veterinarian collection alone is not a sufficient source. The slice therefore adds a read-only SpecialtyRepository (the vet package's narrow Repository style, not JpaRepository), a SpecialtyDirectory value object holding the projection, a thin SpecialtyController, and a new Thymeleaf template. docs/system-design.md Contracts now carries the four REQ-VET-003 rows plus Vet, Specialty and VetRepository; the projection placement is recorded in adr/2026-09-08-specialty-directory-projection-in-a-value-object.md. Coverage claims here rest on grep and direct reads of the vet package, not on the IDE oracle (not connected in this run) — the weaker basis.
integration_points: SpecialtyRepository: new Spring Data interface over the existing specialties table; returns every specialty in name order; extends Repository<Specialty, Integer> with one read method and no write method (NG-2 keeps management out of scope; security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries, least privilege / deny by default). Schema and seed rows already exist per vendor — no schema.sql or data.sql change.
VetRepository.findAll(): reused unchanged as the veterinarian source; it is @Cacheable("vets") and stays so.

SpecialtyDirectory: pure value object, constructed from the two collections, immutable with defensive copies, exposing each specialty with the veterinarians holding it. Unit-testable with real Vet and Specialty instances — no double at this boundary (architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, Value object).

SpecialtyController test — repository boundary double: hand-written stub implementations of SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository, supplied to the @WebMvcTest slice through a @TestConfiguration. Both interfaces are read-only and tiny, so a real hand-written double beats a mock (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy: hand-written doubles before Mockito). Do not copy VetControllerTests' @MockitoBean shape into the new test.
SpecialtyController test — framework transport double: MockMvc, the one sanctioned mock; it drives the real MVC dispatch and view resolution.

Layout fragment: the template calls ~{fragments/layout :: layout (~{::body},'specialties')} with a menu key matching no menuItem in fragments/layout.html. Navigation renders in full (REQ-SYS-001) and no nav entry links to the page or highlights.

patterns.description: lookup-entity repository living inside its feature package, returning rows in name order — the seam SpecialtyRepository copies
the vet package's repository style: narrow Repository<T, ID> with only the read methods the page needs, @Transactional(readOnly = true)
vet-list template: layout fragment call, table markup, and #{...} message keys — the shape specialtyList.html follows, minus the pagination block
one controller per surface family in a feature package; SpecialtyController follows it rather than adding a third route to VetController

risks.risk: Annotating the specialty read @Cacheable("vets") collides with VetRepository.findAll() — both are no-argument methods keyed SimpleKey.EMPTY in the same cache, so the directory would receive a Collection<Vet> where it expects specialties.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyRepository carries no @Cacheable. CacheConfiguration declares only the vets cache (docs/system-design.md § Contracts), and a new cache name would need a CacheConfiguration change plus an eviction answer that is still open (§ Open Questions from the Survey, item 5). Leave both alone.

risks.risk: I18nPropertiesSyncTest.checkNonInternationalizedStrings fails on any literal text in the new template, and checkI18nPropertyFilesAreInSync fails when a new key is missing from any bundle except messages_en.
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing keys specialties, vets and none — they already carry the wording this page needs in all eleven bundles. A genuinely new key must be added to messages.properties and to the nine translated bundles in the same commit (REQ-LANG-002). Specialty and veterinarian names are stored data and are rendered untranslated.

risks.risk: Building the specialty-to-veterinarian grouping inline in the controller is a fresh business rule in a web controller.
risks.mitigation: The grouping lives in SpecialtyDirectory; the controller reads, builds, and returns the view name only. architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog records that the existing controller-rule deviation does not extend to new rules.

risks.risk: The page reads every specialty and every veterinarian on each request and projects in memory.
risks.mitigation: Accepted: the page is unpaged by requirement, the veterinarian read is already cached, and clinic data volume is small. Recorded in the ADR's Consequences.

risks.risk: A new public HTTP entry point on an application with no authentication anywhere (docs/system-design.md § Security Context).
risks.mitigation: The route takes no path variable and no request parameter, so it introduces no input to validate; it reads only and writes nothing. Rendered names are escaped by Thymeleaf's default (§ Threat Model). The route matches the existing posture rather than widening it.

notes: Deviations from the prd-entry's file_targets, which are advisory: (1) a new SpecialtyController rather than a third route on VetController — the Pattern Catalog's Web controller row adapts one HTTP surface, and the naming rule prefixes a controller by its domain noun; (2) a new SpecialtyRepository rather than a Specialty query on VetRepository, which is typed on Vet; (3) tests in new SpecialtyControllerTests and SpecialtyDirectoryTests rather than VetControllerTests, with the four prd-entry test names carried over unchanged and the directory's own cases (a veterinarian under several specialties, a specialty nobody holds) unit-tested against SpecialtyDirectory; (4) messages.properties is expected to stay untouched under key reuse. Open question carried, not resolved: the PRD leaves the order of specialties and of veterinarians unspecified. The design fixes name order for specialties and a stable order for veterinarians under each, for deterministic tests and rendering — a design choice, not a product answer. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain not verified against the NVD in this review: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle, and this reviewer has no network access. The change adds no dependency, so nothing new entered the resolved set; the standing versions are Spring Boot 4.1.1 with the io.spring.dependency-management BOM. A human or CI should close the NVD check separately.

Low-severity resource note: each request to /specialties.html reads the full specialty table (SpecialtyRepository is uncached) and projects it against the full veterinarian set. The vet read is @Cacheable("vets") and the page is unpaged by requirement, so this is bounded by the clinic's data volume and carries no attacker-controlled amplification — worth caching if the specialty table ever grows.
approved_aspects: Output escaping: specialtyList.html renders every request-reachable value through th:text (specialty name, vet first/last name) with Thymeleaf's default escaping on. No th:utext, no fragment-expression preprocessing (__${...}__), no inline JavaScript, no remote resource loading, no href built from model data. A sweep of src/main/resources/templates/ found preprocessing only in pre-existing files (layout.html, inputField.html, selectField.html, vetList.html), none touched by this change.

Data access: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() is a static @Query constant with no parameters and no string concatenation; nothing request-derived reaches query text. Reads are @Transactional(readOnly = true), matching least privilege for a read-only page.

Exposed surface: the new GET /specialties.html takes no request parameter, binds no request body, and exposes only specialty names and vet names already published by /vets.html and /vets. The addition is stated in docs/prd.md and the system-design component table per security-principles.md 'Widening the exposed surface'; no management endpoint exposure changes.

Concurrency: SpecialtyController is a singleton holding only final repository references. SpecialtyDirectory and its nested Listing are records with List.copyOf defensive copies in their compact constructors, and the projection sorts a fresh stream rather than mutating the @Cacheable("vets") collection shared across requests.

Error handling: the only thrown exception (IllegalArgumentException for a Specialty with no stored identity) is unreachable from the controller path, since repository-loaded specialties always carry an id. Its message carries a specialty name — public data, no credential or connection detail — so the error page cannot leak sensitive values.

No new dependency, no build.gradle change, no serialization or Jackson configuration, no file or path handling, no shell execution, no logging, no /tmp use, and no credential-shaped string anywhere in the change set.

No other @WebMvcTest in the suite (VetControllerTests, OwnerControllerTests, PetControllerTests, VisitControllerTests, WelcomeControllerTests) uses `content().string(Matcher)` or imports org.hamcrest — so there is no host-file precedent this file is being 'consistent-with-codebase' with; it introduces a new assertion idiom into the suite.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Purely additive and contained: four new files in the vet package plus one template, one module, no deletions under src, no sensitive paths, and no existing production file modified - the only edits to existing artifacts are docs. The reach beyond the new page is architectural rather than behavioral: SpecialtyDirectory is the first domain-core type in a codebase whose rules otherwise live in controllers, and the ADR states it sets a precedent for later read-model pages.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading all 18 hunks turned up nothing the change's description would not lead you to expect. The grouping in SpecialtyDirectory.of is a straightforward two-collection projection; the holds() identity comparison is null-safe in the one direction that can be null (a vet holding an unsaved specialty yields false, not an NPE) because the isNew() guard fires first on the outer specialty; the compact constructors defensively copy; the projection sorts a fresh stream rather than mutating the cached vet collection shared across requests. The template mirrors vetList.html line for line and reuses only message keys that already exist in all eleven bundles, so no i18n gap opens. Vets are ordered by last-then-first name while the page displays first-then-last - deliberate and documented, not a bug.

test_adequacy.note: Tests are real, not tautological: SpecialtyDirectoryTests drives the projection with real Vet and Specialty instances and uses containsExactly to pin ordering, given-order preservation, multi-specialty membership, the unheld specialty, the omitted non-holder, and the unsaved-specialty rejection; SpecialtyControllerTests asserts against the actual rendered body with hand-written stub repositories, and its doesNotContain assertions would fail against a broken implementation (the word none appears nowhere in the layout fragment, so that assertion is load-bearing rather than incidental). One narrow gap worth knowing: SpecialtyRepository's ORDER BY specialty.name is exercised by no assertion because both controller tests stub the repository, so the system-design claim of name order rests on the JPQL text alone - ordering carries no requirement, so this does not rise to missing coverage of changed behavior.

reviewer_hedging.note: The roster approved unanimously and the test-reviewer's round-1 autofix finding was fixed and cleanly re-approved on the fix-delta, but the security-reviewer's approval carries two recommendations that nothing downstream closes. The first is addressed to the human in so many words: the NVD supply-chain check was not verified because no dependency-check plugin is configured and the reviewer had no network, so a human or CI should close the NVD check separately - the change adds no dependency, which bounds it, but it stays open. The second is a low-severity resource note that every request to /specialties.html reads the full specialty table uncached and projects it against the full vet set. Neither is a correctness doubt; both are residue parked where only this facet reaches the merge decision.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, zero consultations, zero design revisions - the slice never fought its triage. Read against the requirement's stated surface, every Done-when bullet and both new edge cases have a corresponding behavior in the diff, and nothing wanders past them: no nav link, no paging, no second route, no change to the Vet-to-Specialty mapping. The one choice beyond the stated requirement is fixing an order the PRD explicitly leaves open, and the change declares it rather than smuggling it - the ADR names ordering a determinism choice and not a product requirement, and the PRD records the open question.

rationale: Nothing in the diff surprises: purely additive, one module, real tests, no existing production file touched. The residual is reviewer residue, not code. Before merging, read the security-reviewer's two recommendations at handoff line 14 - the unclosed NVD supply-chain check and the uncached full-table read per request - and decide whether either needs an owner.
